chapter_theme: Pambatti's kummi to the snake continues the section on removing inner attachment (அகப்பற்று நீக்கல்): the passions are named one by one as beasts and tools to be mastered (anger the rutting elephant, the mind the horse, desire the sandal, Death the enemy cut down with the kalpa-sword), and against pilgrimage, temple-building, puja, the Vedas and caste the poet sets love, self-knowledge, the guru's foot, the breath at the whirl-point and the light that pervades all like taste in milk.
structure_note: The chapter opens with first-person boasts of conquest over the passions in allegory (2055 to 2061), turns to snake-cipher stanzas on the body and breath (2062 to 2066), then runs a series of attacks on outward religion each paired with an inner alternative (2067 to 2079): pilgrimage, lovelessness, idols and fools, false teachers, temples, scripture, caste and puja. Every stanza ends in the refrain ஆடாய் பாம்பே (dance, snake); the readings give what each stanza adds.

2055.reading: We killed the rut of the mad elephant called anger with the goad of sharp reasoning, and joined in kinship with the red Thing, the form of pure awareness that is called the lamp.
2055.nuance: யுத்தி (reasoning, tactic) is the weapon, not grace or mantra: anger is undone by thinking. சிற்சொரூபம் (the form of chit, awareness) is named as a lamp, and செய்ய பொருள் (the red or right Thing) is the Siddhars' usual name for the Supreme.

2056.reading: We stood firm on the mountain called the eternal, finished what we set out to do and became stainless; truly the one beyond us does not perish, and we shall live for ever.
2056.nuance: நின்மலம் (stainless) is the Siddhanta word for freedom from the malas. எங்கள் கடந்தான் is read here as the one who is beyond us; the line claims both his imperishability and the poet's own unending life, the Siddhar's usual claim to a deathless body or state.

2057.reading: Making the horse called mind our mount, fastening the bridle called intellect in its mouth and climbing properly onto the saddle called anger, we rode off to the place of clarity.
2057.nuance: The horse is explicitly the mind here, not the breath that the Siddhars elsewhere call horse or வாசி; the intellect bridles it. சினமென்னுஞ் சீனி (the saddle called anger) is odd: sitting on anger may mean keeping it under one, or the word may be corrupt.

2058.reading: Setting our foot on the sandal called desire, trampling the thorn-forest of ego to the root, lighting a fire in the bad quality called kaasai, we have passed beyond time and death.
2058.nuance: காசை is unclear: perhaps greed for money (காசு), perhaps a corrupt word. காலாகாலம் கடந்தோம் can mean beyond all time or beyond Kala, Death. Desire is a sandal worn under the foot: used, not renounced.

2059.reading: The fierce and cruel enemy called Death we drove away with the sword called kalpa; we crossed beyond birth on this earth and saw the Supreme.
2059.nuance: கற்பம் is the medical Siddhas' rejuvenating preparation and also the inner practice said to replace it; the verse does not say which, only that it is the weapon against Yama. தற்பரம் is the Supreme beyond the self.

2060.reading: With the mind dissolved like a fly fallen in honey, seeing without bewilderment the vision of the form of awareness, finish the mercury-gem that lets one fly in the sky, put it in the mouth and stand and dance.
2060.nuance: சூதம் is mercury, and tradition reads சூதவான்மணி as a bound-mercury pill (குளிகை) held in the mouth to give the power of flight. A plain reading takes the flying and the gem as figures for the freed mind. The fly in honey is both absorption and being stuck; the verse means the first.

2061.reading: I saw the good raised foot, I saw the light, I saw a dancer within the pure space; the foot set on my bowed head is the foot of the true guru.
2061.nuance: The raised foot is Siva's in the dance (தூக்கிய பாதம்), and the verse makes it the same foot the guru places on the disciple's head at initiation. சுத்தவெளி (pure space) is the inner expanse where the dance is seen.

2062.reading: Snake who lived in the hole at the foot of the banyan, you have entered the hole at the foot of the pipal; look and look at the tip of your tail, draw in and sleep standing, and dance.
2062.nuance: The two trees and holes are cipher: tradition takes the snake as the coiled power or breath moving from one seat in the body to another, and watching the tail-tip as turning back to its root. The plain picture is only a snake changing holes and sleeping.

2063.reading: In four streets stand four pillars, and in the middle street a golden pillar; garland that shining golden pillar with flowers and dance.
2063.nuance: The four streets and the central golden pillar are read by tradition as the nadis or directions and the central channel or spine (the மேரு); the garland is worship of it. Nothing in the stanza fixes this, and the numbers may count something else.

2064.reading: Though the ocean shifts, will Meru be shaken? Even if it were uprooted, even if the aeon of time itself turned, stand with firmness unmoved, according to the truth of knowledge.
2064.nuance: மதி உண்மைப் படிக்கே makes the firmness rest on what the intellect knows to be true, not on will. The syntax of the first two lines is loose; the sense is that Meru does not move for the sea.

2065.reading: Take the wind as your prey and eat it, draw water into the mouth for the ... , let the fire-crescent cool and heat, and in the open expanse join without bewilderment and dance.
2065.nuance: The snake eating wind is the breath practice: வாயு as prey, தேயு (fire) and the crescent (moon) as the sun and moon breaths or heat and coolness, வெட்டவெளி as the open space reached. வருடிக்கு is obscure, perhaps corrupt.

2066.reading: Making a circle in the hole of the stainless path, spreading the great hood that is the moon, praise again and again the primal foot of the faultless Parapara and dance.
2066.nuance: வளை is the snake's hole and also a bangle or ring; மண்டலம் is the coil and also a sphere or a period of practice. The hood as the moon (மதி, also intellect) is cipher tradition takes as the mind or the moon-centre opened; the plain command is to praise.

2067.reading: Running until the legs ache to forests, mountains, rivers, lords and Kasi: can any fruit be seen? To settle in the state that is the way to release, stand at the ghat of Vedanta and dance.
2067.nuance: The list of pilgrimage places is answered by a different துறை (ghat, landing), that of Vedanta: the bathing-place is moved from the river to knowledge.

2068.reading: Those without even a sesame seed of love in the heart never gain release in this old world; cut the bonds of the thieving senses, see and worship Kalakala and dance rejoicing.
2068.nuance: The verse puts love as the condition of release before the restraint of the senses, and names the Lord as காலகாலன், Death's death, so that love and the end of dying are set together.

2069.reading: As frost flees far at the sight of the sun, in the pure place where one's own bonds are scattered, see and behold the noble one, and with love hold him and follow without parting.
2069.nuance: ஆரியன் (the noble one) may be the Lord or the guru; the following and holding fit either. சொந்த பந்தம் (own bonds) is kinship and property, which vanish before the sight like frost before the sun.

2070.reading: Join the stainless mind to the Thing that is seen, as a magnet draws iron and holds it; and in calm, like the pot and its rope, follow without wavering and dance.
2070.nuance: The two images differ: the magnet is attraction that needs no effort, the pot tied to its rope is a bond that does not slip. காட்சியான வஸ்து (the Thing that is seen) makes the object of meditation something already perceived.

2071.reading: Is there any feeling in a chiselled stone image? Is there any feeling in the fools of this world? Does the flaw of copper go by scrubbing with tamarind? Ignorance does not leave the fool.
2071.nuance: The chiselled stone and the tamarind-scoured copper are the stock images of the idol in Siddhar verse; here they serve as comparisons for the fool, whose insensibility is like the stone's and whose fault, like the metal's, does not come off with polish.

2072.reading: Like searching for a needle in a great heap, release is not caught by the teachers of local custom; by the act of the gracious root guru we gained bliss.
2072.nuance: தேசாசார தேசிகர் are teachers of the usage of the country, ritual custom; against them is set the மூலகுரு, the root or first guru. The needle in the heap (போர், a stack of straw) is the futility of searching for release through them.

2073.reading: As a bottle-gourd drawn on a palm leaf is no use for curry, wandering the eight directions does not gain the goal; those who build a temple in every country and worship daily do not see the Lord's feet.
2073.nuance: ஏட்டுச் சுரைக்காய் (the gourd on a leaf) is a proverb for book-knowledge that cannot be used, and the verse applies it to pilgrimage and temple-building: both are representations that do not feed.

2074.reading: Those who know themselves and live by it hide themselves; those who do not know themselves are the ones who show themselves off; such knowers do not think to cherish some other god, for they cherish the great light.
2074.nuance: The second half most naturally continues the self-knowers: the one who knows himself needs no separate god because the great light is already his object. It could also describe the show-offs as men who cherish nothing but display; the first reading fits the chapter.

2075.reading: Standing at the whirl-point in the breath, see the light that spreads everywhere like taste in milk, as ... gold is set to hold gold, and dance rejoicing and rejoicing.
2075.nuance: கால் is read as breath or wind, so காலிற் சுழுமுனை is the whirl-point reached in the breath; it could also be read bodily. பற்றுப்பொன் பற்றவைத்த பான்மை (the way gold is set to catch) is unclear, perhaps gold plating or a goldsmith's solder; the line looks damaged.

2076.reading: Once you have drunk the honey of the sky that overflows and runs, count the bond of the body you took on and this life in the country as vomit, and with great gladness clear your heart and dance.
2076.nuance: வானத்தேன் (the sky's honey) is in tradition the nectar that flows from the head in yoga; the plain reading is the taste of the Supreme. ஓக்காளம் (vomit, nausea) makes worldly life not merely passing but repugnant once that taste is known.

2077.reading: The four Vedas, the six kinds of shastra, the many tantras, the puranas, the arts, the proclaimed Agamas and the various other books: all are vain books.
2077.nuance: The list is exhaustive and includes the Agamas, the Saivas' own scripture; the verse gives no exception and no reason, and its ground is the chapter's: what is known within is not in any book.

2078.reading: The many differences of religion and the differences of caste belong to the people of the world, not to true sadhus; will the mind of those who have climbed the summit change? Learn the Siddhanta of the Siddhas and dance.
2078.nuance: சித்தர் சித்தாந்தம் (the Siddhas' conclusion) is set against the sects' siddhantas; it is a teaching with no sect and no caste. The verse does not abolish caste for the world, only denies it any hold on those who have reached the height.

2079.reading: Does pure awareness come from doing puja? Is there merit in walking round the earth? Resolve that the primal Thing can be reached in the time when desire is gone, and dance.
2079.nuance: The two questions expect no; the positive condition is only ஆசை அற்ற காலம், the moment desire is absent, with no practice named in its place.

links.note: Tirumular tells people to hold the reins of the running horse firmly and drop the garb; Pambatti bridles the horse called mind with the intellect and rides it to clarity. Both make the mind a horse to be reined, and both put that above outward practice.

Bathiragiriyar longs to let the unbridled horse run into the inner space; Pambatti bridles his horse and rides. The horses differ: Bathiragiriyar's is the breath set free, Pambatti's the mind brought under control, the two senses the Siddhars' horse carries.

Kakapusundar says that drinking the kalpa called the self is a samadhi in which one can watch Death's dance from the crown; Pambatti says the kalpa-sword drove off Death. Both make கற்பம் an inner attainment that defeats Yama rather than a drug.

Tirumular says the true guru is the lord who gives his feet, and by giving them grants self-knowledge and quells the bonds; Pambatti sees Siva's raised foot and the light, and says the foot placed on his head is the true guru's. Both identify the Lord's foot with the guru's act of initiation.

Both verses name Kasi as the far end of a futile walk: Bathiragiriyar confesses he went as far as Kasi and wore his legs out instead of watching the breath, and Pambatti asks what fruit comes of running till the legs ache and sets the ghat of Vedanta in its place.

Tirumular says there are many holy waters within the heart and that those who do not bathe there wander over hollow and height; Pambatti lists forests, mountains and rivers run to in vain and names a different ghat. Both move the bathing-place inward.

Tirumular says love itself is Siva and only the ignorant make them two; Pambatti says no one with less than a sesame seed of love gains release. Both make love the condition rather than one practice among others.

Sivavakkiyar says release and siddhi are a pair and tells the reader to recite and realise the Lord with love every day, with the five senses mentioned in between; Pambatti puts love first and the cutting of the senses' bonds second as the way to release. The same two elements in the same order.

Both use the magnet drawing iron, but in opposite directions: Bathiragiriyar asks the Lord to seize and draw him to his feet as a magnet draws iron, and Pambatti tells the practitioner to join his own mind to the Thing as iron to a magnet. Grace pulls in one, effort joins in the other.

Bathiragiriyar asks when the chiselled stone, the red paste and the tamarind-scoured copper will ever become the Real; Pambatti uses the same chiselled stone and tamarind-scoured copper as comparisons for the fool who has no feeling and whose fault will not come off. The idol's images are turned on the idolater.

Tirumular calls false gurus those who have looked over mantra, tantra, yoga and jnana yet do not reflect or make others clear; Pambatti says release is not to be had from the teachers of local custom, and only from the root guru. Both separate the credentialed teacher from the one who gives release.

Tirumular asks what it is to build a thousand temple towers when nothing equals a meal given to a jnani; Pambatti says those who build a temple in every country and worship daily never see the Lord's feet. Both rank temple-building below what reaches the Lord.

Bathiragiriyar calls those who speak knowledge with the mouth and say 'it is I' idle talkers who do not know themselves; Pambatti says those who do not know themselves are the ones who display themselves, while the knowers hide. Both make self-display the mark of not knowing oneself.

Bathiragiriyar asks when he will stand unobstructed in the sushumna between ida and pingala; Pambatti tells the snake to stand at the whirl-point in the breath and see the all-pervading light. The same standing-place, longed for in one and commanded in the other.

Tirumular says there is no dharma that leaves out the Veda and that the wise recited it and gained release; Pambatti lists the Vedas, shastras, tantras, puranas and Agamas and calls them all vain books. On the plain reading of both, one makes scripture the way to release and the other denies it any worth.

Agasthiyar says the four Vedas contradict one another and are a path made in vain for their reciters' livelihood; Pambatti calls the Vedas, shastras, Agamas and all other books vain. Agasthiyar gives a reason (contradiction, self-interest) where Pambatti gives only the verdict.

Tirumular says kin is one and God is one; Pambatti says the differences of religion and caste belong to worldlings and not to true sadhus, and tells the snake to learn the Siddhas' Siddhanta. Both dissolve sect and caste into a single truth, Tirumular's stated flatly and Pambatti's restricted to the realised.

Bathiragiriyar asks when he will go about without any division of caste, as Kapila's agama says; Pambatti says caste differences do not touch true sadhus whose minds have reached the summit. Both make casteless living the mark of the realised, and both ground it in a teaching (an agama, the Siddhas' Siddhanta) rather than in protest alone.

Sivavakkiyar tells those who prepare seats, smear ash and do penances to know where the Lord's knowledge rises and subsides and then do puja, keeping puja on a condition; Pambatti asks whether puja brings pure awareness at all and answers with the end of desire. Sivavakkiyar reforms the rite, Pambatti sets it aside.

source_issues: 2057: சினமென்னுஞ் சீனிமேற் (the saddle called anger) reads oddly and may be corrupt.
2058: காசையெனுந் துர்குணம் has no clear sense; காசை may be a corrupt word.
2065: வருடிக்கு in line 2 is obscure and probably corrupt.
2075: பற்றுப்பொன் பற்றவைத்த பான்மை in line 2 does not parse cleanly and looks damaged.
